core_principles: Push-ups promote shoulder joint stability through muscle cocontraction.
Adjusting hand and wrist positions during push-ups can selectively activate specific muscles to target scapular stability.
Hand position significantly affects the activation of the lower trapezius, upper trapezius, biceps brachii, and serratus anterior.
Lateral hand placement is highly effective for maximizing serratus anterior activation.
specific_findings: Study population consisted of 31 healthy young male participants aged 23.65 ± 0.49 years.
Participants performed push-ups under 11 conditions combining hand position (medial, neutral, lateral), forearm rotation (pronation, supination), and shoulder rotation (internal, external).
Significant effect of hand position on the lower trapezius (p = 0.01, η2 = 0.088).
Significant effect of hand position on the upper trapezius (p = 0.002, η2 = 0.13).
Significant effect of hand position on the biceps brachii (p = 0.003, η2 = 0.132).
Significant effect of hand position on the serratus anterior (p < 0.001, η2 = 0.215), with lateral hand placement exhibiting the greatest activation.
No significant differences in muscle activation were found in the triceps brachii and pectoralis major across the tested hand positions.
